review_note: Independent theorem-only proof-safe review of pinned hypercovering.tex L1125 and Stage A logical fields: For a hypercover of a presheaf G on a site with equalizers and fibre products, the equalizer of degree-zero Čech cochains is H^0(G,F), using sheaf descent over the augmentation. The site and sheaf qualifications remain.
statement:
For an indexed family $\{U_i\}_{i\in I}$ in a category $\mathcal C$, write $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal C)$ for the category of semi-representable families, and let $F$ be the functor sending such a family to the presheaf $\coprod_{i\in I}h_{U_i}$ (hypercovering.tex L110–155).
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with equalizers and fibre products.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a presheaf on $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $K$ be a hypercovering of $\mathcal{G}$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $\mathcal{C}$.
Then $\check{H}^0(K, \mathcal{F}) = H^0(\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{F})$.
For a simplicial semi-representable $K$ and an abelian presheaf $\mathcal F$, $\check H^i(K,\mathcal F)$ denotes the cohomology of the cochain complex associated to the cosimplicial abelian group $\mathcal F(K)_n=\prod_{j\in I_n}\mathcal F(U_{n,j})$ (hypercovering.tex L813–837).
Here $H^i(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ is the $i$th right derived functor of $\mathcal F\mapsto \operatorname{Mor}_{\mathrm{PSh}(\mathcal C)}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ for fixed presheaf $\mathcal G$.

review_note: Independent theorem-only proof-safe review of pinned hypercovering.tex L1181 and Stage A logical fields: The hypercover of arbitrary presheaf G yields a functorial map from Čech cochains to RΓ(G,F), an induced Čech-to-derived cohomology map, and a functorial E2 Čech spectral sequence abutting H^{p+q}(G,F). The presheaf cohomology convention is supplied.
statement:
For an indexed family $\{U_i\}_{i\in I}$ in a category $\mathcal C$, write $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal C)$ for the category of semi-representable families, and let $F$ be the functor sending such a family to the presheaf $\coprod_{i\in I}h_{U_i}$ (hypercovering.tex L110–155).
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with equalizers and fibre products.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a presheaf on $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $K$ be a hypercovering of $\mathcal{G}$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $\mathcal{C}$.
There is a map
$$
s(\mathcal{F}(K)) \longrightarrow R\Gamma(\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{F})
$$
in $D^{+}(\textit{Ab})$ functorial in $\mathcal{F}$, which induces
a natural transformation
$$
\check{H}^i(K, -) \longrightarrow H^i(\mathcal{G}, -)
$$
of functors $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C}) \to \textit{Ab}$. Moreover,
there is a spectral sequence $(E_r, d_r)_{r \geq 0}$ with
$$
E_2^{p, q} = \check{H}^p(K, \underline{H}^q(\mathcal{F}))
$$
converging to $H^{p + q}(\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{F})$.
This spectral sequence is functorial in $\mathcal{F}$ and
in the hypercovering $K$.
For a simplicial semi-representable $K$ and an abelian presheaf $\mathcal F$, $\check H^i(K,\mathcal F)$ denotes the cohomology of the cochain complex associated to the cosimplicial abelian group $\mathcal F(K)_n=\prod_{j\in I_n}\mathcal F(U_{n,j})$ (hypercovering.tex L813–837).
Here $H^i(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ is the $i$th right derived functor of $\mathcal F\mapsto \operatorname{Mor}_{\mathrm{PSh}(\mathcal C)}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ for fixed presheaf $\mathcal G$.

review_note: Independent theorem-only proof-safe review of pinned hypercovering.tex L1260 and Stage A logical fields: For a site hypercover of the terminal sheaf, Verdier's spectral sequence E2^{p,q}=Čech^p(K,underline H^q(F)) converges to global H^{p+q}(F). The matching and Čech definitions and terminal-target convention are retained.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with equalizers and fibre products.
Let $K$ be a hypercovering.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf. There is a
spectral sequence $(E_r, d_r)_{r \geq 0}$ with
$$
E_2^{p, q} = \check{H}^p(K, \underline{H}^q(\mathcal{F}))
$$
converging to the global cohomology groups $H^{p + q}(\mathcal{F})$.
For a simplicial semi-representable $K$ and an abelian presheaf $\mathcal F$, $\check H^i(K,\mathcal F)$ denotes the cohomology of the cochain complex associated to the cosimplicial abelian group $\mathcal F(K)_n=\prod_{j\in I_n}\mathcal F(U_{n,j})$ (hypercovering.tex L813–837).
Here a (non-relative) hypercovering is an augmented simplicial semi-representable object whose target is the terminal presheaf $*$, satisfying Verdier's sheafified covering conditions (hypercovering.tex L1067–1085); $H^i(\mathcal F)$ is site-global cohomology.
